Alex K: heads up — running into inconsistent abort behavior between node sdk AbortController and python context in streaming. node seems to stop immediately, python keeps the connection open until token boundary. anyone seen this?
Miriam R: which endpoints/models? streaming chat or raw completions?
Alex K: streaming chat (delta tokens). node: `controller.abort()` -> stream closes, python: `with cancel_context():` -> server keeps sending a few more deltas then closes. makes client sometimes apply extra tokens after cancel.
Jay: hm, could be how the http client flushes the read buffer. which http lib in py? aiohttp/requests?
Alex K: aiohttp client session with streaming response iterate. code roughly: ```py
async with session.get(url, headers=headers) as r:
    async for chunk in r.content.iter_chunked(1024):
        if cancel_ctx.cancelled: break
        handle(chunk)
```
Noah: are you propagating the signal to the session request itself (timeout/connector)? aborting a user coroutine won't necessarily cancel underlying socket read right away.
Miriam R: also check server keep-alive chunk sizes. small trailing chunks might be buffered. can you paste the minimal repro?
Alex K: repro attached (small gist). main symptom: `await cancel()` triggers app-level cancel but `r.content.iter_chunked` yields two more chunks. node wraps fetch and underlying socket is closed sooner.
Sophie: @Alex K can you try passing `timeout=None` or explicitly closing the response after cancel like `await r.release()` or `r.close()` in aiohttp? that forces socket close.
Alex K: tried `await resp.release()` — that does force immediate close, but felt hacky. wonder if SDK should expose a `stream.cancel()` helper that both calls AbortController and closes response for each language.
sdk-bot: note: issue #2867 created for "stream cancel helper" (assigned: devex).
Jay: agreed — provide an explicit cancel API on streaming iterator for parity across SDKs. Node's `ReadableStream.cancel()` maps to underlying socket close; python needs symmetry.
Noah: also watch retries: if you cancel then a background retry happens, we should ensure idempotency and not re-apply tokens to the application state.
Miriam R: good point — maybe SDK should include a small sequence-numbered chunk envelope so clients can drop chunks after cancel deterministically. but that's a protocol change, heavier.
Alex K: for now I'll add `response.close()` on cancel in python wrapper and open a ticket for nicer API surface. putting the minimal snippet in the PR for review.
Sophie: thanks — tag me on the PR. i'll review streaming ergonomics and consistency matrix for node/py/go.
Jay: small nit — document that `AbortController` in node and `context` in py may differ at socket-level and recommend `stream.cancel()`/`response.close()` patterns until SDK API is introduced.
Alex K: sounds good. quick follow-ups: 1) should we auto-close response in py wrapper when user aborts? 2) backcompat concerns if we change behavior?
Miriam R: 1) yes probably, with an opt-out flag; 2) test matrix needed. add integration test that cancels mid-stream and assert no extra tokens applied.
Noah: i'll add the integration test skeleton. Alex — ping me when your PR is up.
Alex K: will do, thanks all :thumbsup:
Miriam R: (reacts :eyes:)
Sophie: tagging marketing FYI for release notes once we have the new helper API.
